tagline: Copy on iOS, paste on Windows or Linux.
brief: A self-hosted, open-source clipboard relay for developers and power users: copy on the phone, it lands on the desktop within seconds. Lives in the system tray. It should feel instant, light, private and multi-device, without the category clichés (clipboard clip, circular sync arrows, cloud).
criteria: Reads as phone -> computer at a glance, survives 16-22 px as a tray icon in one colour, distinct from blue dev-tool marks.

concepts.name: Phone to laptop
concepts.idea: The piece cut out of the phone has landed inside the laptop: solid and hollow mirror each other, and the orange piece is the clipboard content in transit.
rationale: Phone -> laptop reads at a glance, including at 16 px
Hole and piece face each other across the gap, so the link is visible without arrows
One colour works for the tray; the orange piece carries the brand in colour
Rounded-rectangle geometry on an 8-unit grid, one radius system

recommendation: Final direction: phone to laptop, ink + signal orange.
next_steps: Ship with the next Windows/Linux/iOS releases
